answer: The wander multiplier is published, charged in horizon, and river lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 2508 identities would post 2608 proofs and burn roughly 67 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
